subject: biology
title: Lipids
key_idea: Triglycerides are a glycerol joined to three fatty acids by ester bonds. They are hydrophobic and store energy. Phospholipids replace one fatty acid with a phosphate group, so they have a hydrophilic head and hydrophobic tails, and form membranes.

blocks.text: Triglycerides and phospholipids are two groups of lipid. This section covers how a triglyceride is built.

items.meaning: A small molecule with three –OH groups, to which fatty acids bond.
A hydrocarbon chain with a carboxyl group (RCOOH). R is the hydrocarbon chain.
The covalent bond between glycerol and a fatty acid, formed by condensation.
Repelled by water. Non-polar molecules are hydrophobic.

items: A **triglyceride** is formed by the condensation of one glycerol and three fatty acids.
Each condensation reaction between an –OH of glycerol and the –COOH of a fatty acid forms an **ester bond** and releases a molecule of water.
Three ester bonds form, so three molecules of water are released.
Hydrolysis breaks the ester bonds, using three molecules of water, and gives glycerol and three fatty acids.

rows: C–C bonds in the R group
At least one C=C double bond
Holds the maximum number of hydrogens
Kinked at each double bond, so they pack less closely

items: Triglyceride = glycerol + 3 fatty acids, joined by 3 ester bonds.
Condensation forms ester bonds and releases water.
Unsaturated fatty acids have C=C double bonds; saturated ones do not.

blocks.text: Triglycerides are non-polar, hydrophobic molecules. Their structure explains each of their roles.

rows: Long hydrocarbon chains hold many C–H bonds, so they release a lot of energy per gram, about twice as much as carbohydrate.
Hydrophobic molecules do not dissolve, so they do not affect the water potential of a cell.
Oxidation of the many hydrogens releases a lot of water, useful for desert animals.
A poor conductor of heat, so a layer under the skin reduces heat loss. It also cushions organs.
Less dense than water, so it helps aquatic animals float.

items: Triglycerides are compact, hydrophobic, high-energy stores.
Insolubility means they do not change water potential.

blocks.text: A phospholipid is like a triglyceride, but one fatty acid is substituted by a phosphate-containing group.

diagram.alt: A comparison of a triglyceride and a phospholipid: what they are made of, their polarity and their behaviour in water.
items: Triglyceride
Phospholipid

values: Hydrophilic (polar) phosphate head; hydrophobic (non-polar) fatty acid tails
Does not mix; forms a separate layer
Forms a bilayer or a micelle, with tails facing inwards

items: The phosphate head is **hydrophilic**: it is polar and attracted to water.
The fatty acid tails are **hydrophobic**: they are non-polar and repelled by water.
In water, phospholipids arrange themselves with heads facing the water and tails facing away from it, forming a **phospholipid bilayer**.
The bilayer is the basis of cell membranes. Its hydrophobic centre is a barrier to water-soluble substances such as ions and polar molecules.
Unsaturated tails make the membrane more fluid, because the kinks stop close packing.
Phospholipid = glycerol + 2 fatty acids + phosphate group.
Hydrophilic head and hydrophobic tails make a bilayer in water.

blocks.text: Lipids do not dissolve in water but do dissolve in ethanol. The emulsion test uses this.

items.text: Shake the sample with ethanol so that any lipid dissolves.
Pour the ethanol into water. If lipid is present, it comes out of solution.
A cloudy white emulsion shows lipid. A clear solution means none.

items: Positive emulsion test: cloudy white emulsion.
It works because lipids dissolve in ethanol but not in water.

checks.q: Describe how a triglyceride is formed from glycerol and fatty acids.
checks.a: Three fatty acids each join to glycerol by a condensation reaction. A molecule of water is removed each time and an ester bond forms between the OH of glycerol and the COOH of the fatty acid, giving three ester bonds.

checks.q: Explain the difference between a saturated and an unsaturated fatty acid, and why unsaturated fats are often liquid.
checks.a: A saturated fatty acid has only single C–C bonds; an unsaturated one has at least one C=C double bond. The double bond kinks the chain, so molecules pack less closely and have a lower melting point, so they are liquid.

checks.q: Explain why phospholipids form a bilayer in water.
checks.a: The phosphate head is hydrophilic and faces the water. The fatty acid tails are hydrophobic and face away from the water, towards each other. This gives a bilayer with a hydrophobic centre.

items: Cholesterol is a small lipid with a ring structure. It has a short hydrophilic region (an –OH group) and a large hydrophobic region.
In eukaryotic cell membranes it fits between phospholipids. Its hydrophilic end is near the phosphate heads and its hydrophobic region is between the tails.
It regulates the fluidity of the membrane: it stops it becoming too fluid at high temperature and too rigid at low temperature.
Most prokaryotic cell membranes do not contain cholesterol.
It is also used to make steroid hormones, bile salts and vitamin D.
